Close vgeorge's Diary OSM for Cities at State of the Map Latam 2026 Posted by vgeorge on 31 October 2026 in Spanish (Español) . On 29 October I presented OSM for Cities at State of the Map Latam in Ciudad de México. The project shows how well OpenStreetMap covers a kind of data in a given city, and how recently anyone touched it. The slides are online , in Spanish. Photo by Jordan Jasuta Fischer Most of the talk was a live demo with Mexico City bus stops, coloured by when each one was last edited. When I made the slides, 317 stops had been edited in the past week, almost all along a few routes in the west of the city. Someone was mapping them right then. Most of the rest had not been touched in over 90 days. That is what the platform is for, following a dataset over time instead of looking at it once. Save a dataset and it is refreshed from OSM every day, and a notification arrive by email if it changes. A city team can see when its bus stops get mapped, and a mapper can see whether anyone else is keeping their area up to date. Vector tiles are coming soon Today a dataset loads into the page as one GeoJSON file. That works for bus stops, but not for the buildings or streets of a large city, which is why those are not on the platform yet. Buildings matter most for disaster response and health planning. Mac Ayres: Tiny Desk (Home) Concert November 30, 2020 5:00 AM ET Bobby Carter Credit: Courtesy of the Artist The Tiny Desk is working from home for the foreseeable future. Introducing NPR Music's Tiny Desk (home) concerts, bringing you performances from across the country and the world. It's the same spirit — stripped-down sets, an intimate setting — just a different space. "Tiny Desk! We finally made it!" exclaimed singer-songwriter Mac Ayres as he finished his opening number, "She Won't Stay Long." I'm sure his fans will especially feel that sentiment since they've made a home in our social media feeds and YouTube comments for years now. We were well on the way to hosting Mac Ayres at our D.C. offices until we had to shut down and pivot. As we worked our way through the adjustment to Tiny Desk (home) concerts, he also needed some time to regroup. Sponsor Message The 23-year-old Long Island native shot this in his basement back in September (hence the 'register to vote' comment). Mac's modus operandi lends itself to the Tiny Desk naturally. No over-produced beats, lots of live instruments and a stunning vocal range — and he handles all duties: guitar, bass, keyboard and background harmonies for three songs from previous albums and the premiere of a new song, "Sometimes." pages.text: Visit Kuélap, a Peruvian Archaeological Site a Millennium Older Than Machu Picchu | National Geographic TRAVEL BEST OF THE WORLD Visit Kuélap, a Peruvian Archaeological Site a Millennium Older Than Machu Picchu The remote region north of Lima is also a paradise for lovers of mummies, wildlife, and orchids. At more than 2,500 feet, the Gocta waterfall, near the village of Cocachimba in northern Peru, is one of the world’s tallest. Ernesto Benavides By Heather Jasper Published October 20, 2026 Although the pre-Incan fortress of Kuélap is almost a thousand years older than Machu Picchu, it gets only a fraction of the crowds. The Chachapoya people built the citadel in northern Peru around the year 500 A.D. on a narrow fin of limestone high above the Utcubamba River—not unlike Machu Picchu’s perch above the Vilcanota River. Visit in 2027 to see new exhibits in the Apu Chuillaxa visitors’ center and walk a new trail in Malcapampa , an active archaeological site that has been newly opened to the public. ( See all 25 of the destinations that made our list of the best places to visit in 2027. ) When to Go The warm, rainy season arrives in the cloud forests of this part of Peru in November and lasts until April. More than a thousand orchid species are in bloom and the waterfalls thunder with extra volume. A cooler dry season from May through October offers better road conditions and drier trails, making it easier to visit archaeological sites around Kuélap. The FDA has additional offices across the U.S. Visitors to White Oak can use public transportation (Metro train and bus, commuter trains and buses) or taxi and ridesharing services. Limited visitor parking is available. Please be advised that the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) is conducting baseline water tests at the FDA’s White Oak campus and other FDA locations. They like exploring tight dark places, undeterred by mud and whatever may be lurking. Give a caver a task to do, while down in a cave’s depths, and they will stay underground for hours and come back again a few weeks later to do it again. Who to contact about voter accommodations If you know you will need accommodations to vote in person on Election Day, contact your state or local election office . They can help you understand what to expect at your polling place. Laws and accommodations for voters with disabilities Several federal laws protect the voting rights of Americans with disabilities. These include the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and the Help America Vote Act (HAVA) . Voters with disabilities have the right to: Vote in private, without help Have an accessible polling place with voting machines for voters with disabilities Polling places must have: Wheelchair-accessible voting booths Entrances and doorways at least 32 inches wide Handrails on all stairs Voting equipment for people who are blind or visually impaired If you have a disability, you may: Seek help from poll workers trained to use an accessible voting machine, or Bring someone to help you vote You can also ask your state or local election office what other options you have. Some states offer “curbside voting," when a poll worker brings everything you need to vote to your car. Local organizations may provide transportation to the polls. Know the voter ID laws in your state before going to the polls. Find out if you need to bring an ID to vote Your state's voter ID laws determine whether you will need to show an ID and, if so, what kind. Your state may require you to show a photo ID like a: Driver's license State ID Passport They may ask to see another form of identification like your birth certificate, or Social Security card. If you are a registered voter and have a voter registration card, you are not required to bring it with you when you vote. But you can still use it as a form of identification. Find out what ID your state requires you to bring when you vote. Or learn how to get a voter registration card . How to vote without ID if you are eligible Even if you do not have a form of ID that your state asks for, you may be able to vote. Some states may ask you to sign a form affirming your identity. Find out if you can vote in your state without ID and what information you may need to provide when you vote. Other states will let you cast a provisional ballot. States use provisional ballots when there is a question about a voter's eligibility. They keep your provisional ballot separate until they investigate your eligibility. You may have to return to show an acceptable form of ID within a few days, or the ballot will not count. Learn more about provisional ballots and if you may need to cast one in your state. pages.text: Voting rights laws and constitutional amendments | USAGov Skip to main content Voting rights laws and constitutional amendments Federal laws govern voting rights. Learn about the laws and how they protect your rights and make it easier for you to vote. U.S. election laws date back to Article 1 of the Constitution. This gave states the responsibility of overseeing federal elections. Many constitutional amendments and federal laws protecting voting rights have been passed since then. Constitutional amendments affecting voting rights The 15th Amendment gave African American men the right to vote in 1870. But many weren't able to exercise this right. Some states used literacy tests and other barriers to make it harder to vote. The 19th Amendment , ratified in 1920, gave American women the right to vote. The 24th Amendment , ratified in 1964, eliminated poll taxes. The tax had been used in some states to keep African Americans from voting in federal elections. The 26th Amendment , ratified in 1971, lowered the voting age for all elections to 18. Federal voting rights laws Federal laws passed over the years help protect Americans' right to vote and make it easier for citizens to exercise that right: The Civil Rights Acts created some of the earliest federal protections against discrimination in voting. Covered nonexempt workers are entitled to a minimum wage of not less than $7.25 per hour effective July 24, 2009. Overtime pay at a rate not less than one and one-half times the regular rate of pay is required after 40 hours of work in a workweek. FLSA Minimum Wage : The federal minimum wage is $7.25 per hour effective July 24, 2009. Many states also have minimum wage laws. In cases where an employee is subject to both state and federal minimum wage laws, the employee is entitled to the higher minimum wage. FLSA Overtime : Covered nonexempt employees must receive overtime pay for hours worked over 40 per workweek (any fixed and regularly recurring period of 168 hours – seven consecutive 24-hour periods) at a rate not less than one and one-half times the regular rate of pay. There is no limit on the number of hours employees 16 years or older may work in any workweek. pages.text: Warm-Up Activities Warm-Up Activities Skip Navigation Warm-Up Activities Interact with your students using our 5-Minute Challenge Warm-Up Activities that feature quick, engaging resources that take about five minutes to complete and use real-world Census Bureau data to spark classroom discussion and promote critical thinking. Irish-American Heritage Month How much do your students know about Irish Americans? Test their knowledge with a crossword puzzle and graph showing counties with high Irish populations. Irish-Sounding Places Which states have the most places with Irish-sounding names? These brief, plain-language explanations of FLSA requirements strip away the “legalese” and provide employers the basic information they need to understand their obligations and to comply with the law. We consulted a variety of employers and other stakeholders during the production of these FLSA tutorials, and incorporated their feedback to provide these user-friendly, straightforward primers, delivered in a language and format that’s engaging and easy to understand.
